resources.string: How the cerebellum helps coordinate a reach
A qualitative example of normal reaching. Paths and timing are illustrative.
The brain uses the target location to plan a reach and predicts how the arm will move as the shoulder and elbow work together.
As the hand moves, vision and signals from muscles and joints provide information about where the arm is. This feedback takes time to reach and be processed by the brain.
The cerebellum helps the brain compare the movement it predicted with what the senses report. In this reach, the hand is a little off the predicted path.
The brain can use ongoing feedback together with its predictions to adjust arm movement and guide the hand toward the target.
Across repeated reaches, the cerebellum helps recalibrate predictions for later movements. Here, the hand follows a path closer to the one expected and needs less adjustment along the way.
